title: The shortage is permits, not money
text: A narrow argument that the sector is constrained by permitting rather than by capital: money committed has risen and its cost has fallen, while median permit times have doubled and their variance has grown faster still. Two objections - more applications, and understaffing - are addressed with the observation that the slowest jurisdictions are not the busiest and that two states doubled staff for little gain, because the binding step is sequential review. The recommendation is to run reviews in parallel and publish the queue.
